item.title: Self-Hosted Linux eBPF Firewall Tools: xdp-filter vs bpfilter vs nftables with BPF
item.description: Traditional Linux firewalls use iptables and nftables to filter packets in the kernel networking stack. While effective for most workloads, these tools process packets after they have traversed multiple kernel layers, introducing latency and CPU overhead under high traffic. eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) enables packet filtering at earlier stages — including the XDP (eXpress Data Path) layer, which processes packets before they even enter the network stack.
